clue.text: Tuppence in remuneration occasions rage

indicators.note: in places the coins inside the word for the pay packet

parts.note: remuneration is pay
two old pence, each written D (from the Latin denarius)

explanation.surface: Being paid a pittance makes someone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: D was the symbol for an old British penny, so tuppence (two pence) is DD. PADDY is British slang for a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a paddy is British slang for a temper tantrum, an outburst of anger.

clue.text: Give a ruling before the clerk

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
a scribe is a clerk or copyist

explanation.surface: An official issues a decision ahead of the court clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: To prescribe is to lay down an authoritative rule or direction.

clue.text: Drink for a man on board

definitions.meaning: a swallow or measure of liquid
a piece in the board game called checkers in America

explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a gulp of liquid, and also one of the discs in the British board game of draughts.

clue.text: Still I went after the mythical creature

indicators.note: went after says the letter I follows the word for still

parts.note: still in the sense of 'even so' or 'up to now' is yet

explanation.surface: Someone set off in pursuit of a legendary beast all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti, or abominable snowman, is a legendary ape-like beast of the Himalayas.

clue.text: Car control panel proves a blow to trustees

parts.note: to dash is to strike, so a dash is a blow
a body of trustees is a board

explanation.surface: A setback hits the governing trustees hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument panel in front of a driver holds the gauges and switches.

clue.text: England next in line for recovery

indicators.note: in puts the first two pieces inside the word for a line

parts.note: a string is a line or cord
then means next, as in 'and then'

explanation.surface: England are the next team in the queue to bounce back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' suggests a queue for the throne; here it is a cord, split open to take the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Strengthening, a building back up of power, describes a recovery after weakness.

clue.text: Impudent type

explanation.definitionFit: Bold means cheeky or brazen, and bold is also thick dark print used for emphasis.

clue.text: A Beat poem is in fashion!

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poem by a Beat Generation writer is trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like the 1950s Beat poets, but it is the verb, LAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A la mode is a French borrowing meaning stylish or in the current style.

clue.text: Wild hope of a dunderhead and bore

indicators.note: the head of the word dunder is its opening letter

parts.note: to ream is to bore out or widen a hole

explanation.surface: A fool and a tedious person cherish an unrealistic ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter splits 'dunderhead' in two: the head of 'dunder' gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a fanciful aspiration, a hope unlikely to come true.

clue.text: Lace, it's made to be flexible

indicators.note: made here means fashioned anew, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving three letters

explanation.surface: Lace manufactured so that it stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic springs back after stretching, so it is pliant and adaptable.

clue.text: Join the army and be effective

definitions.meaning: take legal effect, as a new law does

explanation.definitionFit: Entering the armed services literally, and a law becoming valid figuratively.

clue.text: About to get tenancy contract for free

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a lease is a contract granting tenancy

explanation.surface: A tenant is about to sign a rental agreement at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To release is to set loose or liberate.

clue.text: Prison a hundred years old

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
age is how many years old someone is

explanation.surface: A jail building that is a century old.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage is an enclosure for confining a creature, a kind of jail.

clue.text: Twelve noon is correct

parts.note: AM stands for morning, before noon
noon is the end of the morning

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that midday is the right time.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelve noon is the end of the morning, AM END.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to put right or improve by making changes.

clue.text: Returning temper brings ruin

indicators.note: returning means the word for temper is read from back to front

parts.note: a temper or humour is a mood

explanation.surface: A recurring bad temper leads to disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is an unhappy fate or destruction.

clue.text: Bills presented by magistrates

definitions.meaning: British slang for magistrates or judges

explanation.definitionFit: Birds' bills are beaks, and beak is also British slang for a magistrate.

clue.text: Typical measure to attempt to gain access

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of type width
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A standard tool for trying to break in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Typical' here means of type: an EN is a printer's measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry is the right or means of getting in.

clue.text: Then indicates another structure way off

indicators.note: giving the letters another structure means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A building contractor points to a different building far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far away, remote, a long way off.

clue.text: Quieten down when feeling at home

explanation.definitionFit: Having calmed down, and having become comfortable in a new home or job.

clue.text: Buy on tick and get praised for it

definitions.meaning: on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.definitionFit: Taking credit from a seller, and accepting acknowledgement for a deed.

clue.text: Taste butter, and be presented with a puzzle

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste
a ram butts, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: Someone samples some butter and is handed a brainteaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but one who butts: a RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangram is a Chinese dissection puzzle of seven pieces forming shapes.

clue.text: Little right to be in various golf clubs

indicators.note: to be in places the abbreviation inside the word for various

parts.note: divers is an old word for various or sundry
R is the abbreviation, a little form, of right

explanation.surface: A small bit of correctness found among assorted golf equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: DIVERS is an archaic word for several or sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers are long-hitting golf clubs used from the tee.

clue.text: Faint colour one found in high explosive

indicators.note: found in says the numeral sits inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, a high explosive
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A weak hue turned up in a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a pale shade or tinge of colour.

clue.text: Subject Plato picked to deal with in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a part of the words Plato picked

explanation.surface: The theme the philosopher chose to discuss, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or matter for discussion.

clue.text: To a priest it represents evil

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: To a clergyman, it stands for wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: An AFRIT is an evil demon of Arabic myth; 'evil' stands for the evil being.
explanation.definitionFit: An afreet or afrit is a malevolent jinn, a powerful demon in Islamic folklore.

clue.text: What may be needed when Penny gets sick

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny falls unwell and needs something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name; it is P.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet of medicine is what a sick person may need.

clue.text: Space to tie the boat up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to moor is to tie up a boat

explanation.surface: Room is needed to secure the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means space, as in 'room to move'.

clue.text: The French doctor and essayist

parts.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A French physician who also writes essays.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was an English essayist, author of Essays of Elia.

clue.text: Room where father meets Rex with a scowl

parts.note: pa is father
R stands for Rex, king
to lour is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: Dad encounters a frowning man named Rex in the sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rex' looks like a name; it is Latin for king, R.
explanation.definitionFit: A parlour is a sitting room in a house.

clue.text: West Indian ruler given the green light!

parts.note: Goa is a state on the west coast of India
a head is a leader or ruler

explanation.surface: A Caribbean leader is given permission to proceed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Indian' suggests the Caribbean, but it means western India: GOA.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the go-ahead is getting permission to proceed.

clue.text: Cheese constituent consumed by Tom

indicators.note: consumed by says the second word goes inside the first

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a member is a constituent part

explanation.surface: A cheese ingredient is eaten by a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft creamy French cheese from Normandy.

clue.text: Large container containing a small container

indicators.note: containing puts the next pieces inside the word for container

parts.note: a bin is a container for rubbish or storage

explanation.surface: A big bowl that holds a little pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'container' twice on purpose: once in the definition, once for BIN in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a wide bowl for holding liquid.
